answer: In a poll on a raven sculpture at the forge, pairs of registered keys sign election-bound ballots. The server checks signatures and selects a largest set of valid ballots sharing no keys; it rejects invalid and unselected ballots. A signature is a signal of a key holder's support, not identity. Each extra counted ballot needs two more registered keys, potentially requiring recruitment. One person may control many keys, and unmatched voters lose their say.
